<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Define (or revise) the engineered labor standard for a TaskType"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/standards"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



If a standard is already active for this TaskType, it is closed (its effective range ends now) and a new one starts — append-only history, never an in-place overwrite.

A standard may optionally be declared for one handling unit (`handlingUnit`: EACH, CASE or PALLET), so a case handle has its own expected time distinct from an each pick. At most one standard is open per (taskType, handlingUnit): defining a CASE standard never closes the task-type-only one, and revising it closes only the prior CASE standard. A CASE standard may also declare a heavy-case `teamLift` (ADR 0035).

Idempotent retries: clients MUST always send a non-empty `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique value per logical request); a retried request with the same key and body replays the original response byte-for-byte instead of defining the standard a second time.

<ParamsDetails
  parameters={[{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"A caller-minted unique key per logical request (e.g. a UUID). Clients must always send a non-empty key on POST /standards: a retry carrying the same key and an identical body replays the original stored response instead of re-executing the create; the same key with a different body is rejected with 422 idempotency-key-reused, and a missing or empty key is a 400 idempotency-key-required. Postgres is the only runtime, so the check is on in every deployment.\n","schema":{"type":"string"}}]}
>
